last.verdict: EVgo's core charging business is growing fast, but losses and spending are widening, guidance was cut again, and a $2.00-per-share buyout bid from controlling owner LS Power now frames the stock.

takeaways.label: Buyout bid
takeaways.text: LS Power, which holds about 56% of voting power, offered $2.00 per share in cash on November 2. A special committee is reviewing it, and no decision has been made.

takeaways.label: Guidance cut again
takeaways.text: 2026 revenue outlook fell to $375-400M from $400-430M, and the adjusted EBITDA loss widened to $15-30M from $5-25M, the second cut in a row.

takeaways.label: Charging up, rest down
takeaways.text: Charging revenue rose 29% to $72M, but total revenue slipped 1% as partner-built eXtend revenue fell 49%. Per-stall daily use dipped to 283 kWh from 295.

takeaways.label: Losses and cash
takeaways.text: Net loss grew to $49M from $28M a year ago. Cash fell to $99M from $151M at year-end, while debt rose to $312M long-term.

history.verdict: Investors sold EVgo after the company cut its full-year outlook and cash burn rose.

reasons.label: Lower 2026 outlook
reasons.text: Revenue guidance cut to $400-430M from $410-470M; below analysts' roughly $433M.

reasons.label: Bigger expected losses
reasons.text: Full-year adjusted EBITDA now a $5-25M loss, versus a range reaching up to +$20M before.

reasons.label: Cash and slower ramp
reasons.text: Operating cash burn widened and new stalls ramped slower than hoped, despite Tesla deal.
